answer: Pearl Queue requires new agents to join a time-ordered queue, paying a growing delay penalty for each skipped wait period. The mechanism works by making identity acquisition time-bound: each subsequent identity must wait longer than the previous one, costing attackers exponentially more time to generate sybil identities. The per-identity cost is measured in lost opportunity to act, forcing attackers to choose which identities can participate when. The plume of early entrants establishes a trusted baseline while whisper delays prevent mass registration.
